strand_a.title: Geoeconomic Exposure and EU Industrial Policy: Export Dependence Amid US–China Techno‐Nationalist Rivalry
strand_a.summary: Geoeconomic Exposure and EU Industrial Policy: Export Dependence Amid US–China Techno‐Nationalist Rivalry. To illustrate how export dependencies shaped geoeconomic exposure and drove industrial policy dynamics, we then present three short case studies on the positioning of (a) Germany, Spain, and Slovenia in the process of the EU’s imposition of tariffs on Chinese-made EVs, (b) LVMH’s efforts at pacifying the EU’s relations with both the US and China, and (c) Dutch export controls of semiconductor manufacturing equipment. While existing scholarship on how the intensifying geopolitical competition drives the EU’s “new industrial policy” has focused primarily on import dependencies, foreign direct investment, and political/security alliances, we argue that export dependence constitutes an equally consequential yet underexplored dimension of what we conceptualize as geoeconomic exposure.

strand_a.summary: Continuity in times of geoeconomic change: the European Union’s strategic trade relations with the Global South. Various authors depict the rise of geoeconomics as an unprecedented shift in European Union (EU) trade policy, highlighting the entanglement of trade and security goals in a ‘geoeconomic’ agenda that sidelines sustainable development. strategic_pathways.source: European Commission — Defence Industry and Space

lenses.passage: It integrates EU-UA cluster potential through prototyping centre networks, European Defence Fund (EDF) access, supply-chain localisation, reskilling/upskilling, and cluster internationalisation - turning frontline innovation into scalable, export-ready production and strengthening Ukraine's integration into Europe’s defence-industrial and innovation ecosystem. UCA leads Clusters4Defense, an initiative mobilizing Ukrainian and EU clusters as Defence Enablers in the Dual Use/MilTech sectorб https://www.clusters.org.ua/en/clusters4defense-initiative/ .

strategic_classification.trend_action_passage: By joining ENDR, the UCA connects these strengths with Europe’s regional defence ecosystems, supporting a stronger Ukraine and a more secure Europe. Background: Back in July 2026, the European Commission and Ukraine signed a new defence industrial partnership, launched the EU–Ukraine Drone Deal and announced a further €1 billion to support Ukraine’s drone capabilities.

strategic_pathways.title: European Network of Defence-related Regions
strategic_pathways.source: European Commission — Defence Industry and Space
strategic_pathways.authors: European Commission — Defence Industry and Space

lenses.passage: UCA leads Clusters4Defense, an initiative mobilizing Ukrainian and EU clusters as Defence Enablers in the Dual-Use/MilTech sectorб https://www.clusters.org.ua/en/clusters4defense-initiative/ . It integrates EU-UA cluster potential through prototyping centre networks, EDF access, supply-chain localisation, reskilling/upskilling, and cluster internationalisation — turning frontline innovation into scalable, export-ready production and strengthening Ukraine's integration into Europe's defence-industrial and innovation ecosystem.

strategic_classification.trend_action_passage: From 2022 onwards, the ENDR is funded by the European Defence Fund (EDF). ENDR has 3 objectives: Bringing regional organisations and clusters together to exchange best practices on how to develop defence-related development strategies, including the integration of defence industrial and research assets into smart specialisation strategies Facilitating the flow of information for funding opportunities (such as the European Defence Fund, and other EU structural and investment funds); and Promoting the development of regional clusters of excellence.

dynamic_shocks.title: An energy shock hits Europe's Europe's energy supply
dynamic_shocks.plainly: Europe relies on Europe's energy supply. Separate primary evidence shows that an energy-supply shock can change access quickly. Recent weak signals and historical material may strengthen the context, but neither can establish the shock on its own.
dynamic_shocks.second_order: Projects may keep their grants and institutions but still lose time, access or usable capacity while a replacement is found.
dynamic_shocks.why_easy_to_miss: The hypothesis appears when durable European capability evidence and a separately evidenced external pressure are read as one chain; low-weight current signals and history are then used only as context.
reasoning: Primary retained evidence shows European reliance on or expansion of Europe's energy supply.
Separate primary retained evidence shows a live mechanism for an energy-supply shock.
Primary evidence contains 2 direct capability × pressure coupling record(s).
2 recent weak-signal item(s) point in the same direction; each is capped at 30% of a primary evidence item and none satisfies a primary threshold.
2 historical Strand-A item(s) provide structural context; they cannot serve as the current trigger.
The scenario becomes a shock only if the response is slower than the disruption.
conditions: Europe materially depends on Europe's energy supply for current or planned work.
An energy-supply shock reaches the supplier, service, partner or rule that the European capability depends on.
Europe cannot substitute, reroute or absorb the change before projects begin losing usable capacity.
case_against: The primary corpus contains 1 strong sign(s) of substitution, resilience or policy response that could absorb the shock.
Recent media/weak-signal corroboration is intentionally down-weighted and cannot substitute for primary evidence.
The scenario still depends on the disruption arriving faster than Europe can respond.
prevention_actions: Keep several supply routes and suppliers so no single one becomes decisive.
Hold storage and joint purchasing ready before a cut-off.
Keep storage, interconnection and diversified supply ready.
watch_for: Supply through a key route is curtailed.
Energy-intensive producers cut output because of prices.
dynamic_shocks.net_assessment: Well supported enough to watch closely, with contextual signals reinforcing rather than carrying the case.

dynamic_shocks.title: An energy shock hits Europe's critical infrastructure and networks
dynamic_shocks.plainly: Europe relies on critical infrastructure and networks. Separate primary evidence shows that an energy-supply shock can change access quickly. Recent weak signals and historical material may strengthen the context, but neither can establish the shock on its own.
dynamic_shocks.second_order: Projects may keep their grants and institutions but still lose time, access or usable capacity while a replacement is found.
dynamic_shocks.why_easy_to_miss: The hypothesis appears when durable European capability evidence and a separately evidenced external pressure are read as one chain; low-weight current signals and history are then used only as context.
reasoning: Primary retained evidence shows European reliance on or expansion of critical infrastructure and networks.
Separate primary retained evidence shows a live mechanism for an energy-supply shock.
Primary evidence contains 1 direct capability × pressure coupling record(s).
2 recent weak-signal item(s) point in the same direction; each is capped at 30% of a primary evidence item and none satisfies a primary threshold.
2 historical Strand-A item(s) provide structural context; they cannot serve as the current trigger.
The scenario becomes a shock only if the response is slower than the disruption.
conditions: Europe materially depends on critical infrastructure and networks for current or planned work.
An energy-supply shock reaches the supplier, service, partner or rule that the European capability depends on.
Europe cannot substitute, reroute or absorb the change before projects begin losing usable capacity.
case_against: Only one primary retained record currently links the European capability directly to the outside pressure.
The primary direct connection is concentrated in one source, so independent confirmation is still weak.
The primary corpus contains 5 strong sign(s) of substitution, resilience or policy response that could absorb the shock.
Recent media/weak-signal corroboration is intentionally down-weighted and cannot substitute for primary evidence.
The scenario still depends on the disruption arriving faster than Europe can respond.
prevention_actions: Screen ownership and vendors of critical infrastructure early.
Build redundancy and repair capacity for cables, ports and grids.
Keep storage, interconnection and diversified supply ready.
watch_for: Supply through a key route is curtailed.
Energy-intensive producers cut output because of prices.
dynamic_shocks.net_assessment: Plausible, but important parts of the primary trigger or connection still need confirmation.

high_order_inference.lifecycle_policy: Analytical candidates accumulate. One missed detector pass never retires a finding; repeated non-redetection only weakens it gradually, and no new finding automatically deletes an old one.
